_doc: Soviet aviation & strategic threat milestones (1945-1960) driving procedural RFP demand and doctrinal obsolescence.

milestones.name: Tupolev Tu-4 'Bull' Revealed at Tushino Air Parade
milestones.description: Reverse-engineered B-29 gives the USSR intercontinental-range strategic bombing capability.

milestones.name: President Truman Announces Soviet Atomic Bomb Test (RDS-1 'Joe-1')
milestones.description: Ends US nuclear monopoly; triggers urgent continental air defense requirement WS-201A (1954 Interceptor).

milestones.name: Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-15 Appears Over Yalu River in Korea
milestones.description: Swept-wing MiG-15 outclasses straight-wing F-80, F-84, and F9F Panther; accelerates F-100, F-104, and OS-130 F8U.

milestones.name: Soviet Thermonuclear Test (RDS-6s) & Il-28/Tu-16 Jet Bombers
milestones.description: Thermonuclear weapons and Tu-16 Badger jet bombers with anti-ship missiles drive USN Fleet Air Defense (F4H/F8U-3).

milestones.name: Myasishchev M-4 'Bison' & Tu-95 'Bear' Tushino Flyby ('Bomber Gap')
milestones.description: Staged multiple flybys of M-4 Bison bombers trigger the 'Bomber Gap' panic and GOR 114 / WS-202A (F-108 Rapier).

milestones.name: Supersonic MiG-19 'Farmer' & Ye-4 (MiG-21 Prototype) Shown at Tushino
milestones.description: Confirms Soviet operational supersonic fighters and Mach 2 prototypes.

milestones.name: Sputnik-1 Launch & R-7 ICBM Strategic Shift ('Missile Gap')
milestones.description: Soviet ICBMs and SAM networks shift strategic threat away from manned bombers, causing high cancellation pressure on pure Mach 3 interceptors (XF-103, F-108) and SAC escort fighters.
